what_they_do: Walkway sells dynamic pricing software to tour and activity operators (walking tours, museum entries, river cruises, cooking classes, and similar experiences). It pulls in competitor prices, booking pace, and demand signals, then recommends or automatically applies price changes across an operator's full catalog, replacing the manual process of operators setting prices once a year and rarely revisiting them. It connects directly into an operator's existing booking systems and distribution channels so price changes take effect without extra manual work.
vertical: Travel - tours and activities revenue management software
theme_fit_rationale: Walkway continuously reads demand and competitor pricing signals across booking systems and distribution channels and writes price changes back automatically, an always-on cross-system workflow loop that mirrors Theme 2's revenue management use case, applied here to the tours and activities vertical rather than enterprise billing.
workflow_artifacts: booking system and distribution channel integrations

recent_signals.summary: CTO Emmanuel Gautier and VP Terry Donovan published a technical deep dive on the pricing engine: each tour seat is re-evaluated 8 times daily across 7 signals, 2.3M+ price recommendations have been made since the engine launched in December 2025, about 95% of adjustments move prices down or hold steady, and premium price increases backtrack within 36 hours if demand doesn't validate them.
Walkway is hosting a public webinar, "How Dynamic Pricing Works for Tours and Attractions," aimed at operators.
Headcount is up 33% over the trailing 90 days (18 to 24) and 118% over the trailing year, with 6 engineering and 6 data hires currently on the team.
